title: Llegar a: Getting as Far as

sections.content:
You know *llegar a ser* from B1 Unit 39 and B2 Unit 22: the high point of a long road (*llegó a ser patrón*). *Llegar a* + any infinitive works in the same way. It says that someone gets as far as doing something, often after a long process or against the odds.

It has three main uses.
1. A result reached after time or effort: *Llegó a hablar cuatro idiomas*.
2. An extreme, like "even" or "went so far as to": *Llegó a gritarle al capataz*.
3. In *si* clauses, "if it happens to": *Si llega a llover, cancelamos el viaje*. After *si* the verb stays in the present.

sections.title: llegar a + infinitive
rows: Con el tiempo, llegó a hablar cuatro idiomas.
With time, she came to speak four languages.
Estaba tan enojado que llegó a gritarle al capataz.
He was so angry that he even shouted at the foreman.
Si llega a llover, cancelamos el viaje.
If it happens to rain, we cancel the trip.
No llegó a entender la explicación.
He never got as far as understanding the explanation.

sections.content: *Llegar a* + a place is a different verb use you know from A1: *Llegó a la estancia* means he arrived at the ranch. When an infinitive follows *a*, you have the periphrasis, and the idea is a point reached, not a place.
